title: call-stack snapshot propagator for Slack action attachments and annotated postmortems
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Customer-facing incidents and internal SLO alerts frequently lack the immediate context engineers need in the first 10 minutes: relevant span traces, the top-k call stack frames with hotlines, and a compact 'why-this-happened' summary. Current runbook links and raw trace links require clicking through dashboards and manual cut-and-paste. This slows mean-time-to-ack (MTTA) and prolongs blameless troubleshooting.

Goal:
Build a lightweight server-side 'snapshot propagator' that, when an alert or PD escalation is created, captures a compact call-stack + span-summary bundle (top N spans, error-tagged logs, nearest log lines), attaches it to the PagerDuty event and adds an interactive Slack message with: 1) expand/collapse trace snippet, 2) an actionable runbook button (open/runbook-versioned), and 3) an 'annotate postmortem' quick-start that pre-populates the PM template with the snapshot.

Non-goals:
- Full trace replays or storing an additional long-term copy of traces (we will reference existing trace storage).
- Replacing existing runbook authoring flow (we only link and pre-fill).

Acceptance criteria:
- When a PD incident is created for an SLO alert, a snapshot bundle is generated within 6s of incident creation in 95% of cases for incidents with sampling metadata present.
- PagerDuty event shows a link and small JSON attachment with the snapshot bundle (top 10 spans, related log snippets, and error tags).
- Slack incident notification includes an interactive block with a collapsible trace snippet and two buttons: "Open Runbook" (links to current runbook version) and "Start PM Draft" (opens prefilled Google Doc or Confluence with snapshot).
- The "Start PM Draft" flow creates a draft with a stable filename format and returns the draft link in the Slack thread.
- Feature toggled via config (per-customer toggle for Private/Dedicated customers) and off by default for hosted customers under trial.

Design notes:
- Snapshot generator will live in observability-api service and consume the same trace sampling keys used by the runtime. It will call a read-only TraceStore API to assemble the top spans by latency and error score.
- To keep payloads small, snapshots are compressed and include only: span id, parent id, name, service, duration, error tags, top 3 logs per span, and stack frame top 5 entries for each error span.
- Slack blocks will use expanded/summary sections to avoid flooding channels; full trace link still points to tracing UI for deeper debugging.
- For PD, include attachment with metadata and a small 'evidence' JSON in the incident's context field so on-call rotations have immutable context in PD history.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype snapshot assembler endpoint in observability-api that accepts incident_id, sample_keys -> returns snapshot bundle.
2) Add a PD webhook forwarder to call assembler on incident create events and attach returned bundle to PD via PD Events API.
3) Add Slack notifier codepath that posts interactive block with two buttons and uploads snapshot as an attachment to the thread.
4) Integrate with runbook service to resolve the canonical runbook URL and with PM template service to create a draft via API.
5) Add feature flag and per-customer config in config-service and console UI toggle.
6) Add unit + integration tests, and end-to-end test using a synthetic alert pipeline.

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Unit tests for assembler logic and size/latency bounds.
- Staging integration with a dedicated PD team and a Slack workspace used by SRE.
- Canary rollout: enable for internal Redwood SRE and one low-risk customer, monitor MTTA/MTTR, attachment success rates, and payload sizes.
- Full rollout gated on: <1% extra latency added to incident creation path and <5% increase in PD API failure rate during canary.

Metrics to monitor post-launch:
- Snapshot generation latency distribution (p95, p99).
- Snapshot attachment success rate to PD and Slack.
- Change in MTTA/MTTR for incidents with snapshots vs without.
- Bandwidth and storage overhead (snapshot size distribution).

Privacy and security:
- Snapshots must not include raw user PII; assembler will redact log lines matching PII regex and will obey tenant-specific redaction rules.
- Access to full snapshot download restricted to user roles with incident-read scope.
- security_review_required: true

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Large snapshots could cause PD or Slack API rejections. Mitigation: enforce strict size cap (200 KB compressed) and fall back to a short link to the trace UI if exceeded.
- Risk: Sensitive data leakage from logs. Mitigation: redact and require opt-in for Private customers to include less-redacted bundles.

Dependencies:
- TraceStore read API (ENG-41204)
- Runbook service canonicalization API (PM-892)
- PM template draft API (DES-214)
